A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OeMDM/LoMDM research. Their full text, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A–G are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original LoMDM likelihood, zero-shot and generation results, training-dynamics analyses, and scheduler ablations in Section 5 and Appendix F.2.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds model-size and architecture ablations, quantitative scheduler comparisons, and generation-trajectory analysis in Sections 5.3–5.4.

M1.justification: The proposed OeMDM framework and LoMDM architecture, objectives, scheduler parametrization, training algorithm and sampling procedure remain unchanged. The added component-removal and Softmax variants are experimental controls, not replacements for the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use LM1B with and without sentence packing, OpenWebText, and the same seven zero-shot datasets. The added ablations and trajectory diagnostics examine existing language-modeling coverage; conditional generation and QA are discussed only as future work.

E2.justification: The benchmark comparator sets in Tables 1–3 are unchanged. New Table 5 adds evaluated no-stop-gradient and MLP-only LoMDM controls. Table 6 gives explicit Softmax comparison rows, extending the experiment already mentioned qualitatively in v1 Appendix F.1. Newly cited prior methods are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Existing benchmark protocols remain unchanged. Added ablations use 0.5M training steps on unpacked LM1B, including 512/8/8 and 1024/24/16 hidden-size/block/head configurations and scheduler controls. The new trajectory protocol analyzes part-of-speech proportions in 256 length-128 generations over 128 decoding steps, comparing early and late stages.

E4.justification: Sections 5.3–5.4 substantially expand diagnostic evidence through model-size, stop-gradient and scheduler-head ablations, quantitative Softmax tests, and part-of-speech trajectory analysis with Figure 6. The original inference-scheduler ablation remains in Table 3, and the original c1/c2 ablation is retained as Table 8 rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run variability, confidence intervals or significance tests. The added tables continue to report point estimates; the 256 generated sentences specify an analysis sample size, not repeated training runs.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 and the renumbered hyperparameter table retain their values. New 0.5M-step results include LoMDM versus MDLM PPL of 34.3 versus 40.1 for the smaller backbone and 24.6 versus 27.5 for the larger backbone. Architecture and Softmax results add substantive design findings. Table 7 newly shows LoMDM structural-word proportions falling from 0.33 to 0.17 while noun/verb proportions rise from 0.40 to 0.57. Section 5.2 also explicitly reports approximately 50 versus 150 training hours.

T1.justification: The formal definitions, assumptions, NELBO derivations, expressivity proofs and gradient-estimator derivation are unchanged, including Appendices B–E. Changing 'left-most' to 'right-most' masks in the intuitive ARM explanation corrects prose describing the existing construction rather than changing its mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same principal contributions and performance claims. Appendix A newly makes an explicit priority claim that LoMDM is, to the authors' knowledge, the first framework theoretically incorporating jointly learned generation order into MDM training from scratch.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the new ablations as supporting robustness across backbone scales and the benefits of gradient separation and contextual scheduler heads. It adds a structure-first, semantic-content-later interpretation of generation, reports no observed left-to-right bias, and leaves preferred ordering for conditional tasks open. Softmax over-concentration was already discussed in v1 Appendix F.1.

D1.justification: v2 adds a LoMDM code-repository link in the abstract, configurations for the new ablations and trajectory analysis, and explicit training-time figures. Appendix G.1 retains the same preprocessing, tokenizers, optimizer settings, learning rates and GPU specifications.

R1.justification: v2 adds Azangulov et al. (2026), Liu et al. (2026), and Wang et al. (2025). Appendix A adds a focused LO-ARM comparison acknowledging shared goals and analogous objective components while distinguishing autoregressive order modeling from diffusion scheduling and asserting MDM-specific novelty. The broader related-work organization remains intact.

P1.justification: v2 adds Sections 5.3–5.4, expands Appendices A and G.2, adds acknowledgements, updates publication/contact information, shortens the lengthy Llama 3 author list, and makes local wording corrections. Most existing prose and the overall narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: Four new tables display the added ablations and trajectory statistics, and a substantial multipanel Figure 6 visualizes MDLM and LoMDM generation trajectories. Figure 2 is redrawn with revised curve colors and legend presentation. The original hyperparameter table moves and becomes Table 8; existing benchmark tables, other figures and final text samples are retained.

improvement.justification: The new scale and architecture controls provide better evidence for existing design choices, while the trajectory analysis makes learned ordering more interpretable. The LO-ARM discussion and code-access information also improve the paper. These are useful, focused gains over v1's already substantial theoretical and empirical treatment; the added analyses remain limited in scope and provide no run-level uncertainty.
